05b41968.reply: Russia proposed an oral amendment to paragraph 6 of S/2020/24, seeking to replace an explicit list of humanitarian principles with a reference to General Assembly resolution 46/182. Following the adoption of Resolution 2504, Russia withdrew its separate draft S/2020/25. The sequence, tally, and stated reason for the outcome are not provided in the source.

05b41968.source: Russia proposed an oral amendment to paragraph 6 of S/2020/24. It would replace the explicit list of humanitarian principles with a reference to the guiding principles in General Assembly resolution 46/182. After Resolution 2504 was adopted, Russia withdrew its separate draft S/2020/25 in light of that adoption.

08dcb107.reply: The Council voted first on Russia's oral amendment to the Belgium–Germany draft under textual addition/deletion procedures. It received three votes for, seven against, and five abstentions, failing to reach the required threshold. Consequently, the Council proceeded to vote on S/2020/24.

08dcb107.source: The Council put Russia's oral amendment to the Belgium–Germany draft to a vote first under the procedure for textual additions or deletions. It received three votes in favour, seven against and five abstentions and failed to obtain the required number of votes. The Council then voted on S/2020/24.

6f6b785c.reply: Belgium and Germany argued Russia's amendment conflicted with the cross-border mechanism, requesting the Council adopt the penholders' text. They stated no viable alternative existed to Al-Yarubiyah, while the draft asked the Secretary-General to examine alternatives by February's end.

It said there was no viable alternative then to Al-Yarubiyah and that the draft asked the Secretary-General to examine alternatives by the end of February.
